scholarships.title: DAAD Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)
scholarships.official_source: DAAD — German Academic Exchange Service (funded by BMZ)

eligibility: Graduates with at least two years' professional experience from the following countries: list of eligible countries
holds a Bachelor’s degree (normally four years) in a related subject.
has completed an academic degree with far above average results (upper third) and at least two years of related professional experience after the first degree (bachelor) at the time of application.
His/her academic degrees should normally not be more than six years old.
existing.eligibility_summary: Graduates from developing and newly industrialised countries on the DAAD DAC list; at least two years of professional experience; above-average academic results; development-related motivation; must not have resided in Germany >15 months before application.
benefits: Monthly payments: EUR 992/month (Master's) or EUR 1,400/month (PhD, from February 2026)
Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance
Travel allowance (unless covered by home country or another source)
Under certain circumstances: monthly rent subsidy and allowance for accompanying family
coverage: Monthly payments: EUR 992/month (Master's) or EUR 1,400/month (PhD, from February 2026)

documents: Letter of recommendation from current employer
Certificate(s) of employment (at least 2 years after Bachelor's)
existing.english_requirement: Copies of your higher education degree certificates . Please provide a certified translation if the original is not in German or English, and make sure these are clearly legible.
application_method: Apply directly to the chosen postgraduate course (not to DAAD centrally)
existing.best_fit: Young professionals from developing countries seeking development-related Master's or PhD funding in Germany.
existing.notes: Umbrella programme covering separately approved courses; each course has its own deadline and selection committee. Applicants may apply for up to three courses. Applications must be submitted directly to courses, not DAAD.
existing.application_period: Varies by course; applications submitted directly to individual courses
existing.deadline_display: Varies by course (typically August-November annually for next intake)

scholarships.title: Humboldt Research Fellowship
scholarships.official_source: Alexander von Humboldt Foundation (German Federal Foreign Office)

existing.description: The Humboldt Research Fellowship sponsors researchers with above-average qualifications from across the globe to conduct their own research at a German host institution. For postdocs the monthly fellowship amount is €3,000 and for experienced researchers €3,600, plus additional benefits. On top of the fellowship amount the Foundation provides family benefits for children and partners, subsidies for private full health insurance, and travel expense allowances, as well as personal support throughout the sponsorship. The host institute generally receives an allowance for research costs of €800 per month for natural sciences and engineering, or €500 for humanities and social sciences.
eligibility: Postdocs: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last four years?
Experienced researchers: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last twelve years?
Postdocs: have you been published in academic journals and by publishing houses that are reviewed according to international standards?

Experienced researchers: is your academic profile substantiated by an extensive list of publications including important papers in which you acted as thematic lead, and do you hold a leadership role commensurate with your career level (for example assistant professor, lecturer, head of an independent research group or higher)?

If a doctorate in your field or country of origin is not possible or uncommon, you can still apply up to 16 years after completing your master's or other postgraduate degree provided you have a publication record commensurate with your career level.

You are not a German national. If you are a German national, or if you obtained your university entrance qualification and university degree, or your university degree and your doctorate, in Germany, you can apply if you have lived and worked abroad for more than ten years and intend to continue doing so long-term. Have you lived and worked abroad for more than five years? You can still apply if there is a strong connection to your current country of residence (permanent employment, additional citizenship etc.).
For your application to be successful, you may not have lived in Germany for longer than a total of 90 days within the 18-month period prior to submitting your application.

A researcher from an academic institution of your choice in Germany will provide you with a mentoring agreement and written confirmation that research facilities are available, and will compile a detailed review for you.

You can provide two expert reviews. For postdocs: your doctoral supervisor and one other researcher - outside of your institute, if possible. For experienced researchers: important collaborative partners and/or researchers at your own institute as well as other institutes - outside your country of origin, if possible.

Natural sciences and engineering: you must have a good knowledge of German or English. Humanities, social sciences and medicine: you must have a good knowledge of German if this is necessary for conducting your research successfully; otherwise good knowledge of English will suffice.
You may not apply for the Humboldt Research Fellowship if you have already received sponsorship directly from the Humboldt Foundation (research fellowship or award).
existing.eligibility_summary: Postdocs: PhD completed no longer than 4 years prior to application; Experienced researchers: PhD completed no longer than 12 years prior; all nationalities and research areas; must secure a German academic host before applying.
benefits: Monthly fellowship amount EUR 3,000 (postdocs) or EUR 3,600 (experienced researchers)
Family allowance for accompanying spouse/children under certain circumstances
coverage: Monthly fellowship amount EUR 3,000 (postdocs) or EUR 3,600 (experienced researchers)
Family allowance for accompanying spouse/children under certain circumstances
requirements: Submit the necessary documents to the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation online only
You may only submit your application once you have uploaded all required documents in the application form
Two expert reviews must be uploaded in a protected area by the expert reviewers personally; you can only submit once these have been uploaded if the portal is open at that time
Your host will receive a link to upload a host's statement and mentoring agreement; the application is only forwarded to the Foundation once the host has uploaded all necessary documents
Applications that fail to include important documents or information, or that diverge substantially from the specifications, will be formally rejected without further review
documents: Online application via Humboldt Foundation portal
Doctoral certificate or proof of completion
existing.english_requirement: Natural sciences and engineering: you must have a good knowledge of German or English. Humanities, social sciences and medicine: you must have a good knowledge of German if this is necessary for conducting your research successfully; otherwise, good knowledge of English will suffice. No language certificate is required if English or German is your native language. An English language certificate is not required if you have worked in an English-speaking country for several years.
application_method: Online via Alexander von Humboldt Foundation application portal
existing.selection_notes: The decision to award research fellowships is taken by a selection committee consisting of 60-70 researchers from various fields. Applications are academically evaluated by a peer review process based on: academic career and academic record to date (mobility, determination, thematic scope, academic productivity); quality of the key publications named in the application; originality and innovative potential of your proposed research; your future potential; and your independent research profile (for experienced researchers). The assessment also considers the individual life journey and educational background in terms of equal opportunities and accessibility. The Foundation expects 20-25% of the applications received to be approved.
existing.best_fit: Postdoctoral and early-career researchers seeking to conduct research in Germany.
existing.notes: Part of the Global Minds Initiative Germany. Calls open 8 months before selection meetings. Once call reaches 800 applications, it closes until next round. Postdoc fellowships last 6-24 months; experienced researcher fellowships last 6-18 months.
existing.duration: Postdocs: 6 to 24 months, divided into up to three stays within three years. Experienced researchers: 6 to 18 months, divided into up to three stays within three years.
existing.application_period: Three selection rounds per year (March, July, November)
existing.deadline_display: Three calls annually: March 15, July 15, November 15 (2026 schedule)
